title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
description: Six Flags Magic Mountain, in Valencia, California, is a hillside thrill park known for a very large coaster collection spread across steep terrain. Its operating headliners include the hybrid Twisted Colossus, the flying coaster Tatsu, the rotating-seat X2, the launched Full Throttle, and the steel giant Goliath, alongside family areas and shows. The park's history is written in replacements: the original wooden Colossus was reborn as Twisted Colossus, while Deja Vu and Flashback are retired names that older visitors still recall.
lands_areas: Bugs Bunny World, DC Universe, Thrill Capital areas, Samurai Summit, The Underground
rides_new: NEW (operating): Twisted Colossus (hybrid coaster); Tatsu (flying coaster); X2 (4D coaster); Full Throttle (launched coaster); Goliath (steel coaster)
theming_ecosystems: Thrill-capital theming: superhero districts, a mountain summit village, and a cartoon family land sharing one hillside park
hidden_spots: Publicly-known hidden spots: the shaded paths of Samurai Summit, the quiet overlooks above the lower park, and the back walkways between the mountain coasters

demo.code:
RIDES = [
    ('Twisted Colossus', 45),
    ('Tatsu', 40),
    ('X2', 50),
    ('Full Throttle', 35),
    ('Goliath', 30),
]
print('Wait-time estimate: Six Flags Magic Mountain')
total = 0
for name, wait in RIDES:
    total += wait
    print('%s: %d min' % (name, wait))
print('Rides listed: %d' % len(RIDES))
print('Total queue time if ridden once each: %d min' % total)
print('Average wait: %.1f min' % (total / len(RIDES)))
longest = max(RIDES, key=lambda r: r[1])
print('Longest wait: %s at %d min' % longest)
demo.expected_output:

X2: 50 min

title: Six Flags Great Adventure
description: Six Flags Great Adventure, in Jackson, New Jersey, is a large park paired with a drive-through safari, and its coaster lineup mixes a celebrated wooden coaster, El Toro, with tall steel rides like Nitro and the single-rail Jersey Devil Coaster. Its past is just as famous: Kingda Ka, once the world's tallest coaster, and Green Lantern both closed after the 2024 season, and the old wooden Racing coaster Rolling Thunder closed in 2013. The park keeps reinventing its skyline while its frontier, movie, and boardwalk districts carry the day-to-day family visit.
lands_areas: Main Street, Frontier Adventures, Movie Town, Golden Kingdom, Plaza del Carnaval, The Boardwalk
rides_new: NEW (operating): El Toro (wooden coaster); Nitro (steel coaster); Jersey Devil Coaster (single-rail coaster); Batman The Ride (inverted coaster); Superman Ultimate Flight (flying coaster)
rides_past: PAST: Kingda Ka (2005-2024); Green Lantern (2011-2024); Rolling Thunder (1979-2013)
theming_ecosystems: Safari-adjacent adventure theming: a frontier town, a movie-stunt district, a golden temple area, and a boardwalk midway
hidden_spots: Publicly-known hidden spots: the quiet lakeside paths near the frontier area, the shaded seating behind the boardwalk games, and the back route between the movie district and the golden temple area

demo.code:
RIDES = [
    ('El Toro', 10, 45),
    ('Nitro', 9, 40),
    ('Jersey Devil Coaster', 9, 35),
    ('Batman The Ride', 8, 30),
    ('Superman Ultimate Flight', 8, 30),
]
print('One-day itinerary: Six Flags Great Adventure')
plan = sorted(RIDES, key=lambda r: -r[1])
clock = 10 * 60
for name, thrill, wait in plan:
    hh, mm = divmod(clock, 60)
    print('%02d:%02d ride %s (thrill %d/10, wait %d min)' % (hh, mm, name, thrill, wait))
    clock += wait + 15
hh, mm = divmod(clock, 60)
print('Plan ends about %02d:%02d after %d rides' % (hh, mm, len(plan)))
demo.expected_output:
One-day itinerary: Six Flags Great Adventure
10:00 ride El Toro (thrill 10/10, wait 45 min)
11:00 ride Nitro (thrill 9/10, wait 40 min)
11:55 ride Jersey Devil Coaster (thrill 9/10, wait 35 min)
12:45 ride Batman The Ride (thrill 8/10, wait 30 min)
13:30 ride Superman Ultimate Flight (thrill 8/10, wait 30 min)
Plan ends about 14:15 after 5 rides

title: Six Flags Fiesta Texas

title: Six Flags New England

Its operating headliners include Superman The Ride, the hybrid Wicked Cyclone, the classic wooden Thunderbolt, the inverted Batman, and the spinning Pandemonium. title: Six Flags Astroworld
description: Six Flags Astroworld, in Houston, Texas, operated from 1968 until 2005 as part of the Astrodomain beside the Astrodome, and it is recorded here as a past park, not an operating one. Its retired coasters include the wooden Texas Cyclone, which ran from 1976 to 2005, the looping Ultra Twister, the suspended XLR-8, the shuttle-loop Greezed Lightnin', and the Viper. The park closed at the end of the 2005 season and the site was later cleared, so the park survives in photographs, home movies, and fan histories.

title: Six Flags New Orleans
description: Six Flags New Orleans, in Louisiana, opened in 2000 as Jazzland and operated as Six Flags New Orleans from 2002 until Hurricane Katrina struck in 2005, after which it never reopened as a park. Its retired coasters include the wooden Mega Zeph, Batman The Ride and Jester, both later relocated to other parks, and the boomerang-style Zydeco Scream. The site has stood closed since, and the park is recorded here as a past park whose story is inseparable from the storm that ended it.
